name: Minimum Flip-Flop Count / Counter Design
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai mod-N counter (ya specific counting sequence) ke liye MINIMUM flip-flops kitne chahiye — direct formula-application pattern.
whatShouldComeToMind: Johnson counter: 2n states from n flip-flops. Ring counter: n states from n flip-flops — different formulas, don't confuse with standard binary.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify N (the modulus or number of distinct states in the target sequence).
2. If it's a standard binary counter: apply ⌈log2(N)⌉ directly.
3. If it's specified as Johnson or ring counter: apply the special n↔state-count relationship instead.
variationsObserved: Custom counting sequence given explicitly (not just 0 to N-1) — count the DISTINCT states in the given sequence, apply ⌈log2(distinct count)⌉.
Gray-code-style constraint (at most 1 FF changes per transition) — same flip-flop count formula applies, but NEXT-STATE LOGIC design differs.
commonTraps: Using the standard log2(N) formula for a Johnson/ring counter question instead of their specific formulas.

name: Counter State Sequence Trace / Analysis
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek counter circuit diya hai (flip-flops + next-state logic) aur poocha hai counting SEQUENCE kya hai, ya specific initial state se agli states kya hongi — is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (17 me se 7 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Build the next-state table from the given circuit's logic (J-K/D/T flip-flop excitation equations), trace step by step from the given initial state.
conceptsRequired: Flip-flop excitation table application (J-K, D, T)
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Write down each flip-flop's next-state equation from the given circuit/logic.
2. Starting from the given initial state, apply the equations to compute each subsequent state.
3. Continue tracing until the requested number of states/full cycle is found.
variationsObserved: Saturating up/down counter (stops incrementing/decrementing at boundary values instead of wrapping) — special-case the boundary transitions explicitly.
Mixed flip-flop types (some D, some JK) in the same circuit — apply each flip-flop type's own excitation table correctly.
commonTraps: Applying the wrong flip-flop's excitation table (mixing up J-K vs D vs T behavior) when multiple types coexist in one circuit.
edgeCases: Saturating counters: verify the exact boundary behavior (does it hold at max, or wrap?) as specified.

name: Counter Timing / Max Clock Frequency Analysis
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai maximum clock frequency kya hai given propagation delays (flip-flop, gates, setup time) — ye timing-analysis pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Identify the CRITICAL (longest) path between clocked stages — sum ALL delays along it (flip-flop propagation + any combinational gates + setup time).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Trace the circuit to find the LONGEST delay chain between any two clock edges (through flip-flops AND any combinational logic like AND gates feeding the next flip-flop).
2. Sum all delays along that critical path, add setup time.
commonTraps: Only counting the flip-flop's own propagation delay, forgetting to include any combinational logic (AND gates, etc.) that sits between flip-flop stages on the critical path.

name: Counter Equivalence / Conceptual Combinations
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai counter+decoder combination kis equivalent circuit jaisa behave karta hai, ya counter ko DFA/register-based circuit ke roop me interpret karna hai — ye conceptual-combination pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Trace the counter's full state cycle FIRST, then apply the attached decoder/logic's mapping to see the overall combined effect.
conceptsRequired: Counter-cycle tracing combined with downstream logic mapping
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Determine the counter's full state cycle independently.
2. Apply whatever downstream combinational logic (decoder, register operation) is attached, for EACH state in the cycle.
3. Identify the overall equivalent behavior/pattern from the combined trace.
